add: uv add --group dev '{pkg}=={version}'   # omit --group for a runtime dependency
post_add_fixup: Two hazards, both measured. (1) Never pass --exclude-newer when bumping an existing lock: it re-resolves the whole graph -- one dev patch bump moved 94 packages, including uvicorn, pandas and mcp. Verify the date with check_cooldown.py instead; --exclude-newer belongs on `uv add` for a brand-new dependency, where a full resolve is expected. (2) Omit --group and uv writes a dev tool into [project.dependencies] as a runtime dep, leaving the real entry in place. Always diff pyproject.toml.

cooldown.note: Nothing enforces this at install time. Dependabot's own cooldown covers the PRs it opens; a hand-typed version or a transitive pin is unguarded. Do not reach for --exclude-newer on a bump -- see post_add_fixup.

transitive_pin.note: constraint-dependencies bounds an existing transitive dep without adding it as a direct one; override-dependencies forces a version against a parent's stated requirement. Prefer the former.

metrics.name: tests
metrics.note: Counts FAILURES, lower-is-better, like imports and lint -- not tests run. A green suite matches nothing and scores 0 via exit 0; '1 failed, 244 passed' scores 1, which is the point. No -q here: pyproject addopts already sets it, and -qq suppresses the 'N failed ... in Xs' summary this pattern reads -- a real failure then scores UNMEASURABLE instead of a count.

baseline_tools_note: ruff produces the lint count and pytest the test count. A ruff bump can add rules, so a changed count is expected -- read the new findings rather than trusting the delta.
